text:
maria: Autopromote for release v2026.03.18 kicked off. Canary at 10% but traffic controller paused after errors — Istio 503s and a bunch of pods never came up in the new nodepool. Argo shows the terraform step failed during apply.

aj: Can you paste the error from the terraform job?

maria: Here — from the infra CI job: 
```
Error: Error creating Subnet: AddressLimitExceeded: The maximum number of addresses has been reached for the subnet.
  status code: 400, request id: 9f2b-xxxx

  on vpc.tf line 42, in resource "aws_subnet" "canary":
  42: resource "aws_subnet" "canary" {
```

argo-bot: ArgoCD sync: application/infra-autoscaled-nodepools failed to sync: resource aws_subnet.canary: CREATE_FAILED

deploy-bot: Traffic-split controller paused automated promotion at 10% and initiated rollback to stable (reason: canary unhealthy).

sanjay: So the rollout never actually got the new pods, traffic was rolled back — good from availability perspective but noisy. Who approved creating new subnets in the same AZ? That AZ is near exhaustion.

lex: Confirming — our subnet in us-west-2a is at 98% allocation. New nodepool creation tried to carve more IPs and hit quota. We either request a quota/IP increase or place nodes in another AZ.

aj: Quick mitigation: can we patch the canary helm values to set nodeSelector to existing nodepool so pods schedule without new nodes? Minimal change to get a real canary running.

maria: I tried that — patched the helm release but Argo immediately reported drift. Patch command I ran: 
```
kubectl patch deployment llm-canary -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector","value":{"pool":"shared-legacy"}}]'
```

jules: That will create a drift vs GitOps. We can do temporary manual patch with an annotation `gitops/temporary: true` so the auto-sync ignores for 30m. But we should update terraform/helm properly afterwards.

lex: I pushed a small helm override in the staging values to use shared-legacy nodepool and bumped canary % to 5% for safety. Argo shows app out-of-sync; I'm creating a short-lived manual sync to avoid races.

argo-bot: Application llm-service is OUT_OF_SYNC for 18s (diff in values.yaml -> canary.nodeSelector). Manual sync started by lex.

aj: Note for post-mortem: our progressive delivery automation treats any canary probe failures as app-level health failures and triggers rollback. It doesn't distinguish scheduling/errors from runtime errors. We should update the controller to look at pod scheduling state (Pending & NotReady due to InsufficientIPs) and pause promotion instead of instant rollback.

maria: Agreed. Immediate actions: 1) keep rollback (already in place) to protect production; 2) temp-patch canary to run on shared nodes so we can re-run a controlled canary; 3) open AWS support ticket for subnet/eni increases and confirm AZ capacity.

sanjay: Also add a Terraform plan-time guard so nodepool creation is only attempted if target AZ has capacity (or create in a different AZ). We had assumptions baked into the module.

jules: I'll file a PR to change the autopromote orchestration: if scheduling-related failures > 60s, do not auto-rollback but mark canary as "blocked" and notify oncall. We can tune thresholds before enabling.

maria: Will monitor the manual sync. If the shared node canary comes up okay at 5% for 15 min, we'll resume autopromote with a 10-min cool-off.

lex: One more ops note — cost: creating many small subnets in all AZs increased our IP fragmentation. For future capacity, prefer nodepool autoscaling within existing subnets, or consolidate subnets with larger CIDRs in infra templates. I'll add to infra backlog.

aj: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident doc and link the Argo/CD job + terraform logs.

maria: TL;DR: rollout paused by autopromote due to subnet IP quota during nodepool create -> caused pods not to schedule -> traffic controller rolled back. Mitigation: manual nodeSelector patch to shared nodes, temp manual Argo sync, request quota bump, and change autopromote health logic to treat scheduling errors as "blocked" not immediate rollback.

jules: filing followups: INFRA-721 (subnet sizing), INFRA-722 (autopromote health state), INFRA-723 (GitOps safe-override pattern).

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 2026-03-18T16:07:41Z :white_check_mark:

maria: marking this thread for postmortem notes. Will attach logs and timeline in the doc. :spiral_note_pad:
